steps.tx: **Autoimmune polyendocrine** syndrome type 1, APS-1, also called APECED, is autosomal recessive AIRE disease. The classic triad is chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism, and Addison disease, and two of the three make the diagnosis. It presents in childhood. The drawing places candidiasis and hypoparathyroidism on this side only.

vis.alt: Drawing of autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1 with AIRE, candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism, and Addison disease in childhood, beside type 2 with Addison disease, thyroid disease, and diabetes in adults.
vis.caption: The drawing puts candidiasis and hypoparathyroidism on the type 1 side. Type 2 is drawn as adult Addison disease with autoimmune thyroid disease, with or without type 1 diabetes (StewardMD).

steps.tx: **Autoimmune polyendocrine** syndrome type 2, APS-2, is Addison disease plus autoimmune thyroid disease, which is Schmidt syndrome, with or without type 1 diabetes, which is Carpenter syndrome. It is polygenic and HLA associated, and it presents in adults. Candidiasis and hypoparathyroidism are not part of it. Type 3 is thyroid disease without Addison disease, so that figure is the wrong diagnosis.

right.title: Type 2

steps.tx: **IPEX syndrome** is FOXP3 deficiency in boys, with infancy-onset diabetes, severe enteropathy, and eczema. Haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation is the disease-directed treatment. Insulin does not fix the enteropathy. This is not autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1, and AIRE is the wrong gene.

steps.tx: **CTLA-4 blockade**, as with ipilimumab, is the checkpoint class most likely to cause hypophysitis, and the ACTH loss is often permanent. PD-1 or PD-L1 blockade more often causes a thyroiditis that is thyrotoxic and then permanently hypothyroid. Name the drug class before you promise that the axis will recover. The toxicity drawing does not name which drug hits which gland.

steps.tx: **Checkpoint inhibitor** diabetes is insulin deficient. It often presents with diabetic ketoacidosis, GAD antibodies are sometimes present, and it is usually permanent. Metformin is not the treatment, because this is not ordinary type 2 diabetes. The toxicity drawing shows the pituitary and the thyroid with rash, lung, heart, liver, and gut injury, and it does not name the drug class.

vis.alt: Drawing of immunotherapy toxicity affecting the pituitary and thyroid, with rash, pneumonitis, myocarditis, hepatitis, and colitis.
vis.caption: The drawing shows pituitary and thyroid injury together with rash, lung, heart, liver, and gut toxicity. It does not name CTLA-4 blockade or PD-1 blockade (StewardMD).

steps.tx: **Primary adrenal** insufficiency from immunotherapy is uncommon and life-threatening. A cortisol level is taken before the fatigue is blamed on the cancer. Hydrocortisone is given if the patient is unstable, and the ACTH result is not required before the first dose. A low cortisol in a shocked patient on a checkpoint inhibitor is adrenal failure until it is proved otherwise.

nodes.label: Unwell patient on a checkpoint inhibitor
Take cortisol before blaming the cancer
Do not wait for the ACTH result

steps.tx: **High-dose** glucocorticoid for hypophysitis reduces mass effect, and it rarely restores ACTH secretion. Levothyroxine is started in the hypothyroid phase, and it is not stopped only because immunotherapy is continuing. Endocrine toxicities usually do not require stopping a cancer drug that is controlling the disease. Replace the missing hormone and keep the oncology plan.

steps.tx: HIV can **cause** a **euthyroid** sick pattern, opportunistic adrenalitis from tuberculosis or cytomegalovirus, and lipodystrophy from older antiretroviral drugs. A low cortisol in advanced HIV is adrenal insufficiency until it is proved otherwise. Do not file a low cortisol as the euthyroid sick pattern. That pattern explains the thyroid tests, and it does not explain an undetectable cortisol.
